data.description: Arctos record identifiers or GUIDs (of Arctos collections) when used as identifiers, are used primarily to form relationships. Only Arctos record identifiers may be used here; Arctos record identifiers cannot be used with other identifier types, except Arctos:Entity when used as Organism ID. Automation will correct issued_by agent, and will estimate the DarwinCore triplet rather than GUID if provided.

This type is proper for a wide range and majority of identifiers. Most should be disambiguated by the agent that issued them (Issued by agent). Resolvable identifiers which are less-precise than "Arctos record GUID" or "Organism ID" belong here.

Probable misuse of field number. Treated as a label.

Field number, aka station number (typically applied to ship/marine collections) is intended to be an identifier assigned to a collecting event. Treated as a label. Sometimes used as a synonym of collector number, and may reference collector's notes. Fish collections/collectors use the standard for field numbers set by Hubbs and Lagler, 1947--- i.e., an alphanumeric with collector's initials, last two digits of year, and 001 to infinity...then start again next year (001 to ?). E.g., AMS17-021. Treated as a label.
Treated as a label. Media; as useful as "ink on paper."
Treated as a label. Media; as useful as "ink on paper."

DO NOT USE: misuse of field number. "Sub-field number" assigned to traps or other capture apparatus when a locality or event encompasses multiple such devices. Several individuals or cataloged items may share both this identifier and any of field number, collecting event nickname, or locality nickname. The use of more precise locality and/or event data should be heavily preferred when possible.

metadata.label: Identifier Types
metadata.description: Types of identifiers assigned to catalog records that are useful when a specific Issued By agent is assigned to the identifier value. Broadly, Identifiers that are URL (web links) conform to the Extended Specimen Network concept (Type A) and all others do not. See https://handbook.arctosdb.org/documentation/identifiers.html for more information and usage guidelines.
